AUDIT_STATUS: CORRECTED - control now exists; K6/K8 are fidelity-neutral, not better than BF16
AUDIT_NOTE: The missing BF16-embedding control has been measured under byte-identical env with the canonical fidelity.py replay: 0.0026488 mean, 0.027320 p99, 0.978220 top1 (receipts/trellis-embed-bf16-control-2026-08-22.json). Against that control: K8 +0.17%, K6 +0.69% - both inside this repo's 0.94% kernel-routing noise band, so both are FIDELITY-NEUTRAL, not improvements. K4 is +7.87% mean / +10.14% p99, the only resolvable cost. The earlier claim that K6 (0.002667) beat BF16 embeddings (0.002700) is retracted: 0.002700 was an offline number from a different harness, and the true same-harness control is 0.0026488, which K6 is slightly WORSE than - as physics requires.
title: Trellis K4/K6/K8 Embedding Round-Trip KLD
method: EXL3 trellis round-trip on embed_tokens [248320, 5120] via quantize_exl3 (uncalibrated, meta Hessian) + ext.reconstruct + hadamard_fold_weight, injected into vLLM V1 model via collective_rpc, hidden states captured and replayed against BF16 reference through shared BF16 LM head. Same 512-context v5 shard-0000 suite as int8/int6/FP8KV tests.
suite: fp8kv-evidence/capture-suite-view (512 contexts, 2047 positions each, 1,048,064 scored positions)

comparison.notes: Trellis embeddings are BF16-sized in this round-trip test (no memory savings). The trellis payload would be ~4, 6, or 8 bits per weight but the production path requires a reconstruct_rows kernel (issue #435).

key_findings: Trellis K4 embedding KLD (0.002857) is 7% worse than int8 (0.002667) but still 16% better than int6 (0.003409).
Trellis K6 embedding KLD (0.002667) is essentially identical to int8 (0.002667) — same mean KLD to 6 significant figures.
Trellis K8 embedding KLD (0.002653) is marginally better than both K6 and int8 — 0.5% lower mean KLD.
Trellis K4 p99 (0.03009) is 9% worse than int8 (0.02754) but 13% better than int6 (0.03476).
Trellis K6 p99 (0.02729) is slightly better than int8 p99 (0.02754) — 0.9% lower tail error.
Trellis K8 p99 (0.02709) is the best of all five — 1.6% lower than int8.
All three trellis variants (K4/K6/K8) beat int6 on both mean KLD and p99 KLD.
Proxy error scales as expected: K4=0.005772, K6=0.000324, K8=0.000019 (18x and 17x improvements per 2-bit step).
The Hadamard-folded trellis round-trip preserves embedding quality at least as well as per-row int8 quantization at K6+, validating the trellis coding approach for embeddings.

Production use requires implementing the reconstruct_rows kernel for row-indexed gather (issue #435), since the existing reconstruct kernel requires 128-row alignment and is designed for full-matrix dequantization, not scattered row access.

technical_details.encoding: Chunked along V (vocab) dimension in 97280-row chunks (3 chunks for 248320 rows) to avoid quantize_exl3 CPU-swap path (numel > 5e8 triggers weight_r.cpu() which breaks device assertion in fallback_quant). Hadamard fold is block-diagonal (128x128), so chunking with multiples of 128 is equivalent to full-matrix encoding.
technical_details.process_split: Pre-encode runs in a separate podman container (releases GPU on exit), then capture runs in a second container that loads vLLM and injects the pre-encoded embedding via collective_rpc. This avoids EXCLUSIVE_PROCESS mode conflict where the pre-encode CUDA context blocks vLLM's EngineCore spawn.
technical_details.hook: Inline forward hook on language_model.model.norm captures hidden states in bf16 with accumulate mode for chunked prefill (ctx_len=2112 > max_num_batched_tokens=2048).
